title: Dynamic span throttler with per-tenant SLO feedback loop
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Problem:
Current tracing emits a high volume of spans for noisy routes and tenant bursts which increases p99 latency and GC pressure in the hot path. Recent perf regressions traced to span allocation and sync commits have amplified cost for busy tenants. We need a lightweight, adaptive throttler that reduces emission volume without losing fidelity for SLO/incident detection.

Goal:
1) Reduce per-request hot-path allocations from tracing by 40-60% for top-100 noisy routes.
2) Maintain detection rate for high-severity errors and tail latencies (alert fidelity >= 95%).
3) Provide per-tenant emission budgets and automatic backpressure that respect tenant SLOs and burst allowances.

Design overview:
- Local admission controller in the ingress/service-side tracer that decision-samples spans based on a two-tier budget: a short-term burst token bucket (ms scale) and a longer reservoir (minute scale) per-tenant.
- Probabilistic scoring: incoming span gets a priority score based on route latency delta, error flag, and sampled risk (rare endpoints get higher base weight). High-score spans always pass. Lower-score spans pass with p= f(score, budget).
- Feedback loop: controller subscribes to a lightweight SLO monitor stream (per-tenant p95/p99 latency and error rate) from metrics pipeline. If a tenant's tail metrics exceed thresholds, throttle relaxes and reservoir refills faster; if under-utilized, throttler tightens.
- Async low-cost emit path: spans that are not admitted can be optionally aggregated as compact summaries (route/error/latency histogram) and emitted on a timer to preserve aggregate signal for dashboards. This reduces full-span write amplification.
- Hot-path optimizations: use object pooling for span headers, zero-copy references for immutable parts, and move encoding/IO to bounded background workers to eliminate sync calls on the request critical path.

Rollout and safety:
- Feature flag per-cluster and per-tenant. Start in shadow mode (control decisions made but all spans emitted) for 1 week to validate detection fidelity.
- Canary: opt-in 5% of tenants with high traffic; monitor tracing emission rate, p99 end-to-end latency, and alerting signal.
- Fallback: automatic disable if p95 latency increases by >2% or if alert fidelity drops below 95% for any canary tenant for >10 minutes.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end trace emission volume reduced by >=50% for the noisy route cohort in canary tenants without reduction in error/incident detection.
- Hot-path allocations attributable to tracing reduce by >=45% on sample service (benchmarked under synthetic load).
- Dashboards show preserved tail signal: detection of injected high-latency events in shadow and canary matches baseline >=95% of the time.
- No more than 1 rollback during the canary window; rollback procedure documented and automated.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- New dashboard: "Span Emission Controls" (per-tenant): emission-rate, reservoir-fill, burst-usage, admitted-vs-aggregated spans, and decision-reason histogram.
- SLO feedback metrics: feedback-lag, hysteresis-events, throttle-adjustments.
- Incident playbooks: steps to force-disable throttler, collect aggregated summaries, and re-run with increased shadow duration.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Week 1: implement admission-controller core, token buckets, and probabilistic scorer (unit tests & microbench).
- Week 2: integrate SLO signal subscription and implement feedback loop; add compact-aggregator flush path.
- Week 3: optimize hot-path allocations, instrument metrics, and add feature flags; run synthetic benchmarks.
- Week 4: shadow + canary rollout, observation, and iterative tuning.

Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood/company/obs/throttler-design (draft)
- Benchmark PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/6142
- Prototype server PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tracing/pull/189

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Over-throttling causes missed incidents. Mitigation: shadow mode + strict canary gating and aggregate summaries to preserve signal.
- Risk: Increased complexity in config per-tenant. Mitigation: sane defaults and automatic tiering based on historical emission rates.
- Risk: Feedback oscillation. Mitigation: add hysteresis and rate-limit adjustments in the control loop.
